sample.name: decocms
sample.purpose: Self-hostable MCP gateway, AI-provider credential management, and web UI

verdict_evidence: The entire BP1 gateway-key storage class is byte-identical in downloaded npm release 4.509.1 and the sample. It selects one organization's subsidized_gateway_keys.encrypted_key, decrypts it with the application's vault, and supplies it as the deco provider apiKey. put() encrypts and upserts the same credential.
Both archives contain 7,333 members. Common-name changes are package.json (version only), dist/client/index.html (hashed asset links), and dist/server/server.js. Bundled dependencies do not change.

After normalizing minified identifiers and template-expression identifiers, the meaningful server changes are two GitLab JSON-response parsing call sites, extraction of the canceled/denied order-monitor row helper, and the embedded package version.

Client assets matched as multisets after normalizing Vite chunk hashes have only three changed logical bundles: the main bundle's cache buster and two UI bundles' displayed/current-session version strings. All change 4.509.1 to 4.509.3.

The earlier archive also fires the pre-edit encrypted-key rule under the current engine. Thus the queue's earlier no-detection observation does not establish that this key access was introduced in 4.509.3.

provenance.record: npm SLSA statements link the archive digests to decocms/studio main and .github/workflows/release-studio.yaml. Their signatures were not independently verified; the behavior comparison is the decisive evidence.

reverse_engineering.execution: Static source and syntax-tree comparison; application/server and untrusted network payload entry points were not executed.
reverse_engineering.unicode_layer: Inspected the server's unicode-escape@5642219 finding and source/literal facts. The recovered text is adjacent ordinary application code, including the same gateway-key query, not a concealed payload.
reverse_engineering.captcha_api: The flagged constructors are part of Huffman/DEFLATE lookup-table construction. fS, fT and fU alias Uint8Array, Uint16Array and Int32Array. In fY, iD is a numeric Uint16Array and new fU(iD[0x1e]) allocates the numeric reverse table. This does not establish a string table.
reverse_engineering.captcha_paint: Isolated and evaluated only the pure string-table function, RC4/base64 decoder, and rotation in QuickJS with memory/time limits. Decoded 1,797 distinct call expressions and statically folded adjacent strings. The payload program was not executed. Its __cf_wapi result gathers browser navigator, canvas/WebGL, storage-support, and display properties. Genuine string-array obfuscation remains suspicious; that is compatible with an anti-bot service.
reverse_engineering.github_react: Traced the fetched react-core router's URLSearchParams iteration and hard-navigation location.replace. Its ordinary query/default/index processing is unrelated to concealment; the old whole-file combination overclaimed obfuscation.

trait_corrections.reason: Own-application encrypted key selection is not evidence of attacker collection. Literal regex, confidence, and JS/TS platform scope are unchanged; unsupported T1005 mapping removed.

Matcher establishes indexed constructor-argument syntax, not string contents or concealment. Regex, count, confidence and platform scope preserved. Removed the objective-level obfuscator exclusion because metadata cannot depend on objectives and the syntax remains accurate inside obfuscated code; this only broadens the supported syntax observation.

trait_corrections.disposition: Removed unsupported aggregate; expanded its two required conditions in both attack-specific consumers.
trait_corrections.reason: Co-occurring indexed constructor arguments and Function(call()) do not establish a string table feeding Function. Both supported constituent observations remain.

trait_corrections.disposition: Removed unsupported aggregate; expanded its original all/any conditions in all three phishing consumers.
trait_corrections.reason: An alternative is plain location.replace beside ordinary query forwarding. No obfuscation or shared value flow is required. Existing query/navigation atoms remain; no attack condition was dropped.

Records the paint module's computed screen-property reads into width/height fields. Requires screen indexing in a dimension-field initializer, not a generic layout-object read. Does not claim screenshot capture or surveillance.

consumer_audit: Updated both exact encrypted-key exfiltration references and the two webhook source consumers that previously selected the query through objectives/collection/.
Expanded the indexed-constructor/Function conjunction into the cloud/GitHub credential-sweep and self-defending loader consumers.
Expanded the query-iteration/navigation conjunction/disjunction into all three CAPTCHA phishing consumers, preserving their other requirements.
Reviewed objectives/collection parent suppressors and objectives/anti-static/obfuscation parent consumers. Neutral observations were not reinserted as intent or concealment evidence.
The new source-syntax observation's only ancestor selector is a PHP-only source-form profile; its JS-only scope cannot enter that consumer.
The new screen trait's sole broad screen-directory consumer is Python-scoped, so the JS/TS trait does not activate it.

CAPTCHA error/expiry completion with decryption and dynamic navigation (three consumers)
AWS/GitHub credential sweep with eval and Function generation
benign_controls: separate indexed Function constructors and call-result Function generation
plain and computed query/window calls without deceptive CAPTCHA context
coverage_verification.existing_corpus_review: Searched existing rule consumers and test fixtures, inspected 565 archived/compressed JS/TS/HTML controls, and inspected scripts in the two outside-batch Baileys archives and ordinary/concealed wallet ZIPs. No existing positive fixture for these exact retired atomic matchers was found. Coverage equivalence was then tested with explicit hostile controls rather than inferred from benign near misses.
coverage_verification.real_dependency_controls: Re-scanned real CaptchaFox API/paint and GitHub react-core files. Genuine paint string-array obfuscation remains; API typed-array syntax and React router operations retain their neutral observations.
coverage_verification.presentation_note: The query-iteration OR helper can disappear as a redundant standalone finding when its erroneous aggregate consumer is removed; its direct loop atom remains and the attack consumers continue to require it.

deployment_context: No deployment authorization, configuration, or observed runtime was supplied. The verdict rests on the packaged program's actual purpose, unchanged owned-key access, and ordinary release diff; generic execution/network/crypto capabilities and legitimate obfuscation are retained.
validation: Eleven focused controls passed. Final gate: make validate (must exit 0 with no warnings before completion).

scan_comparison.material_detection_loss: No supported behavior coverage lost in the tested artifacts or hostile controls. Five package/dependency suspicious occurrences of unsupported claims were replaced or removed. The final scan also omitted one neutral GitHub asset due to the four-URL fetch budget; an independent identical-byte scan with original and final rules retained all its findings.
scan_comparison.classifier_disagreement: None: both scans are calibrated benign (lvl=-1; class 0). The remaining genuine CaptchaFox obfuscation is not a malicious-package verdict.
scan_comparison.model_diagnostic: The installed model is v18.18 while the extractor reports newer version-19 features; the scanner warns about zeroed forward-compatible features. No evidence here demonstrates a classifier miss.

fetch_budget_reconciliation.reason: The final scan exhausted its inherited four-URL request budget before this asset; this is not a rule-induced loss.
fetch_budget_reconciliation.resolution: Fetched the exact asset independently, verified its SHA256 equals the pre-edit asset, then scanned it with the original and final rules at the same hashed basename. All original traits remain and no suspicious/hostile finding appears.
